title: Default judgment
text: When a defendant fails to plead, default procedures may permit judgment after the court examines jurisdiction and the requested relief.

title: Late opposition
text: A district court may enforce a briefing deadline and decline to consider a late opposition memorandum.

title: Material dispute
text: A factual disagreement prevents summary judgment only if the fact is material under the governing law.

title: Evidence at judgment
text: The court considers admissible evidence and draws reasonable inferences for the party opposing summary judgment.

title: Unopposed motion
text: An unanswered summary judgment motion is not automatically granted. The court must still decide whether the moving party demonstrates no genuine dispute of material fact and a right to judgment as a matter of law.

title: Burden of proof
text: A party bearing the burden at trial must identify evidence supporting each essential element challenged by a properly supported motion.

title: Pleading standard
text: A complaint must allege sufficient factual matter to state a plausible claim for relief.

title: Discovery extension
text: A party seeking additional discovery must identify the facts it expects to obtain and explain why they are needed.

title: Local rules
text: Local briefing rules regulate deadlines, but do not relieve a court of applying the governing substantive standard.

title: Review on appeal
text: An appellate court reviews the grant of summary judgment without deference to the district court legal determination.

title: Sanctions
text: Before imposing severe discovery sanctions, a court considers the conduct and the availability of lesser measures.

title: Personal jurisdiction
text: The exercise of personal jurisdiction requires sufficient connections between the defendant and the forum.

title: Hearsay
text: An out-of-court statement offered for its truth generally requires an applicable exception to be admissible.

title: Affidavit
text: An affidavit supporting a motion must be based on personal knowledge and set out facts that could be admitted in evidence.

title: Credibility
text: At summary judgment, weighing evidence and resolving witness credibility belong to the fact finder at trial.

title: Contract interpretation
text: An unambiguous contract is construed according to the ordinary meaning of its terms.

title: Statutory deadline
text: A statutory filing deadline may bar an otherwise sufficient claim when no exception applies.

title: Injunction
text: Preliminary injunctive relief requires a showing of likely success and irreparable harm among other factors.

title: Standing
text: A plaintiff must establish a concrete injury traceable to the challenged conduct and redressable by relief.

title: Venue
text: A transfer determination accounts for the convenience of parties and witnesses and the interests of justice.

title: Waiver
text: Arguments not presented to the district court are ordinarily not considered for the first time on appeal.

title: Service
text: Proper service gives a defendant notice of the proceedings and an opportunity to appear.

title: Judgment as law
text: After a party has been fully heard, judgment as a matter of law may follow where a reasonable jury lacks a legally sufficient basis to find for it.

title: Reconsideration
text: A motion for reconsideration is not an opportunity simply to repeat arguments already rejected.

title: Qualified immunity
text: An official may be protected from damages unless the alleged conduct violated a clearly established right.

title: Claim preclusion
text: A final judgment on the merits can preclude the same parties from relitigating the same claim.

title: Removal
text: The removing party bears the burden of establishing the federal court subject matter jurisdiction.

title: Expert opinion
text: Expert testimony must rest on reliable methods applied to sufficient facts and assist the trier of fact.

title: Jury instructions
text: Jury instructions are assessed as a whole to determine whether they accurately convey the governing law.

title: Costs
text: Recoverable litigation costs depend on the governing statute and the court exercise of its discretion.
